einzeiler: Why a former White House advisor resigned over hidden corruption and lobbying in D.C.
kurzfassung: Calley Means discusses his resignation from the Trump administration as a senior White House advisor leading MAHA initiatives. He details how powerful lobbyists and officials like Susie Wiles systematically blocked popular health policies and protected corporate interests. Furthermore, he explains why structural reform is urgently needed to address systemic corruption in American politics.
stichpunkte: Resignation from the White House due to intense frustration with systemic lobbying and corruption
Extreme centralized control by Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and political operatives tied to special interests
Surprising executive order and DOJ actions granting legal immunity and protection for glyphosate
Pushback and lobbying efforts against school lunch reforms and defining ultra-processed foods
Political strategies focusing heavily on midterm polls and fundraising rather than fulfilling voter promises
High prevalence of chronic diseases, pre-diabetes, and obesity among American children linked to dietary incentives
Widespread revolving door culture where government officials and advisors transition directly into high-paying lobbying roles

clips.hook: Kratom is a straight-up opioid causing devastation
clips.text: An unregulated herbal substance sold easily in retail shops functions identically to dangerous narcotics and ruins lives.

clips.hook: The day I left, junk food company stocks went up 8%
clips.text: Corporate markets reacted immediately with financial gains when policy advocates for healthier food were pushed out.

beschreibung:
Calley Means is a health advocate, author, and former senior advisor to the United States Department of Health and Human Services. He is also a co-founder of Truemed and co-author of the book "Good Energy" with his sister Casey Means, MD.
